\begin{chapstatus}{The thread of this chapter}
Memory is a hierarchy: small and fast near the processor, large and slow far away, and locality makes the trick work. Next: the third part of Verm1, which needs memory for a whole body.
\par\medskip\textbf{Exit ticket} (two to four minutes, alone, on paper):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item What happens on a cache miss? Why does a loop that reads an array in order have few misses?
\item Why can't the firmware and the cartridges of the kit live only in RAM? Which memory keeps them, and what is its limit?
\end{enumerate}
\end{chapstatus}
